chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He who guarantees four [qualities] with four [verses/verses of guidance] will be in Paradise: Spend [in the way of God] and do not fear poverty, and do justice to the people from yourself [even if it is against you], and spread the greeting of peace throughout the world, and leave argumentation even if you are right.

key_terms.أَبْيَاتٍ: houses or verses (here metaphorically referring to the four items)
key_terms.أَنْصِفِ النَّاسَ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ: do justice to people from yourself (give them more than their due)

ai.seo_question: What are the four qualities that guarantee entry into Paradise according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links specific social ethics to the ultimate reward of Paradise, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with communal harmony. The instruction to 'spend and fear not poverty' echoes the concept of *kafalah* (guarantee) by Allah, while the directive to leave argumentation even when right highlights the virtue of *hilm* (forbearance) over mere factual correctness.
